one-step-equations.why: An equation is a balance. Whatever you do to one side you do to the other, and it stays true. Solving means undoing operations until the unknown is alone — and you undo in the reverse of the order they were applied.
traps: Undo with the inverse operation. To clear ~+7~ you subtract 7; to clear ~\times 7~ you divide.

two-step-equations.why: Work backwards through the order of operations: the thing done last is undone first. In ~3x + 5 = 20~, the 5 was added last, so it comes off first.
traps: Dividing before clearing the constant is legal but produces fractions unnecessarily. Clear the constant first.

multi-step-equations.why: Simplify each side fully before you start moving things across. Multi-step equations are not harder in kind, only in bookkeeping, so one line per step is the whole technique.
traps: When a bracket is multiplied by a number, either distribute it or divide the whole equation by it — but do not do half of each.

variables-both-sides.why: Collect the unknowns on one side and the numbers on the other. Moving the smaller coefficient keeps the remaining number positive, which removes a whole class of sign errors.
traps: Subtracting a term from both sides is the same move as 'moving it across and changing the sign' — they are not two rules.

equations-fractions.why: Multiply every term by the least common denominator and the fractions vanish. Doing this first is almost always faster than carrying fractions through the whole solution.
traps: *Every* term must be multiplied, including the ones with no fraction in them.

special-solutions.why: Sometimes the unknown cancels out. If what remains is true (~5 = 5~), every number works — the two sides were the same expression. If it is false (~5 = 8~), nothing works. Neither case is an error; both are answers.
traps: 'No solution' and 'the solution is 0' are completely different. ~x = 0~ is a perfectly good solution.

equation-word-problems.why: Four steps, always: define the variable in a sentence, write the equation, solve it, then answer the question that was asked. The middle step is the easy one.
traps: If you defined ~x~ as the smaller number, make sure the final answer is the quantity the question wanted.
